fixes.explanation: Paul, an apostle writing to the believers in Ephesus (Ephesians 1:1), says, “…I urge you to walk in a manner worthy of the calling you have received…” He writes this as a prisoner, and he calls himself an ambassador in chains (Ephesians 6:20). I think that gives his words extra weight. A man in chains is asking about the walk, not the view.

Paul says the opposite. Everything in these verses is "one": one body, one Spirit, and they were called to one hope. Many paths would sound nice and roomy, but it's not what he writes. One hope is the number he gives.

Not in this verse, baker. Paul says they were called to one hope when they were called. He puts it right beside one body and one Spirit. Separate callings aren't in the verse, and gifts don't get handed out until later in the passage.
Paul describes the one God and Father of all as the One “…who is over all and through all and in all.” Over, through and in, friend. Three little words, and I find them comforting.

Paul says, “Now to each one of us grace has been given according to the measure of the gift of Christ.” Each one, baker. Paul counts himself in that "us," and a stamper from the back of a junk drawer happily does too.
Paul gives a different reason. He says the One who ascended did it “…in order to fill all things.” The verse gives the reason, and leaving the earth behind isn't it.

I'd have guessed a nap too, friend, but that's not the reason Paul gives. He says the One who ascended above all the heavens did it “…in order to fill all things.” Resting doesn't appear in the verse, and filling does.

Verse 11 says, “And it was He who gave some to be apostles, some to be prophets, some to be evangelists, and some to be pastors and teachers…” So apostles and prophets are the first two on the list. Evangelists, pastors and teachers follow right behind them, baker.
Those two aren't on Paul's list. Verse 11 names apostles, prophets, evangelists, and pastors and teachers. Kings and priests never show up in the verse. Paul's list is about people given to the body.
Not in this verse, friend. Paul lists apostles, prophets, evangelists, and pastors and teachers. Judges and elders don't appear in it. Checking a list against the text is a good habit, baker.

Plot twist, baker: that one is true. Paul says they were given to equip the saints for works of ministry and “…to build up the body of Christ…” Building up is right there in the purpose, plain as flour on an apron.

Paul doesn't call it harmless. He says infants are “…tossed about by the waves and carried around by every wind of teaching…” Then he adds “…the clever cunning of men in their deceitful scheming.” That doesn't sound harmless, baker.

Paul says, “Instead, speaking the truth in love, we will in all things grow up into Christ Himself, who is the head.” Paul puts truth and love together in one phrase, friend. Speaking the truth is the job, and love is how he says to do it.
Paul doesn't say that. He says to speak “…the truth in love…” Nothing about secrecy is in the verse. Speaking the truth is the job, and love is how he says to do it.
Paul says the whole body “…grows and builds itself up in love through the work of each individual part.” Each part, baker, not just a few. I'm just a small stamper, and I'd say that's good news.
